name: Open Source Collective
summary: US nonprofit, not a charity, that hosts open source projects from anywhere in the world. Its requirements are written for software; its licence standards include the open hardware principles.

evidence.quote: That includes software projects, open source advocacy groups, open source meetups, open source conferences, open source research efforts, and more
OSC is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(6) nonprofit that supports the infrastructure needs of open source projects.
Because we are a 501(c)(6), OSC is not a registered 501(c)(3) charity; donations to hosted member projects are not tax-deductible.

projects.value: Open source projects of all kinds

evidence.quote: Open Source Collective (OSC) welcomes open source projects of all kinds - from anywhere in the world, in any language (spoken or programming).

gate.value: Not a charity: some grants go only to 501(c)(3) charities

evidence.quote: Some grants are restricted to 501(c)(3) organizations. Open Source Collective is a 501(c)(6) nonprofit, so before applying, confirm that the grant you're interested in allows funding to a 501(c)(6).
welcomes open source projects of all kinds - from anywhere in the world

value.note: anywhere in the world, except where US embargoes apply

evidence.quote: welcomes open source projects of all kinds - from anywhere in the world
Open Source Collective (OSC) charges a fixed 10% host fee on incoming funds.

fees.value: No setup fee, minimum balance or recurring charge

evidence.quote: There are no setup fees, minimum balances, or recurring charges to be part of OSC.
We use third-party payment processors, such as Stripe, PayPal, and Wise, which apply their own processing fees to incoming donations and outgoing expenses.

fees.value: It keeps the interest on your money

evidence.quote: All interest earned on the Fund which will be retained in OSC's general fund.

fees.value: With its payroll: $50 per employee a month, plus US provider fees of $49-$99 and typically $250 a year for insurance

evidence.quote: PEO/EOR Fees $49-$99 per employee per month (U.S.), depending on benefits status. International quotes available upon request Insurance Coverage under OSC's employment liability insurance (typically $250 per year, varies by project type) Administrative Fee $50 per employee per month

min_income.value: May not suit projects expecting under $600 a year in donations

evidence.quote: Expect to receive less than $600 USD in donations annually Smaller projects may find other platforms more suitable

value.note: OSC receives the money and has to be involved from the early stages.

evidence.quote: When your project applies for a grant, OSC acts as the receiving organization on your behalf. Grant funders pay us, and we deposit the funds into your account on the platform, where you can use them for reimbursements or invoices just like any other contribution. Because we're the receiving organization, we need to be involved from the early stages of your application

value.note: employment contracts, payroll and benefits, in countries its provider covers; contractors otherwise

evidence.quote: Employees must be located in one of the countries covered by our PEO provider and be legally allowed to work in that country. For other types of work, projects may hire independent contractors

conditions.value: An open source licence; the standards it follows include the open hardware principles

evidence.quote: Your project must use an open source license that clearly defines how it can be used, modified, redistributed, and referenced by others. We follow the licensing standards from: Open Source Initiative Approved License List Free Software Foundation License List Debian Free Software Guidelines Fedora Software License List Open Source Hardware Association Statement of Principles

conditions.value: In an organisation’s repository, not a personal account

evidence.quote: The project must be hosted under an organizational repository, not a personal account.

conditions.value: Recent activity, or a significant degree of use

evidence.quote: The project should show recent activity and/or have a significant degree of usage.

conditions.value: No business income for one person or client

evidence.quote: We are not structured to process business income intended for individual benefit or specific client transactions.

conditions.value: Funds are held in US dollars only

evidence.quote: As a U.S. nonprofit, we only hold funds in USD.

conditions.value: No payments to countries under sanctions

evidence.quote: As a U.S., organization, we cannot process payments to sanctioned countries

conditions.value: Not based where it is illegal to provide services from the US

evidence.quote: Your Collective is not based in a country where it is illegal to provide services from within the USA.

conditions.value: Never the main awardee on a US National Science Foundation grant

evidence.quote: We can help with National Science Foundation (NSF) grants, but there's a structural limit to our involvement. OSC can only act as a secondary awardee (subawardee), never as the primary awardee.

steps.value: Check the terms, fees and eligibility

evidence.quote: Read our Terms of Fiscal Sponsorship Agreement Review our fees so that you understand the costs involved Checked that you meet our eligibility requirements

steps.value: Apply, with GitHub or manual verification

evidence.quote: We have two different methods of application: GitHub verification and manual verification.

steps.value: Review, which it aims to do weekly

evidence.quote: We aim to review incoming applications weekly.
Have, preferably, 2 community members ready to be added as admins on the Open Collective page.

own_entity.value: OSC’s money can’t go to a related LLC or its costs

evidence.quote: Projects with an associated LLC cannot use funds held by OSC for LLC-related expenses or transfer donated funds to the LLC.
